# Map widget image rendering issues (2026-01-12 11:46Z)

_**User**_

I have tested the new version intensively on a physical device and I have found that the map widget still seems to have issues as in: it is not always showing the correct map-image, even though the text and distance of the map-widget has updated correctly and shows "updates n seconds ago..." with the correct location/distance.

Why would the map pre-render-to-image of the map widget break?
What could be done to prevent this and reliably render map widget maps?

### Why the widget map image can “lag” while text is correct (most likely causes)

Here are the hypotheses I want to prove with runtime logs (not guesses):

- **H1 – Two writers racing/overwriting the same PNGs (most likely)**  
  You have **two snapshot generators**:
  - App: `miataru/views/Common/WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator.swift`
  - Widget: `miataruWidgets/WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator.swift`  
  Both write to the **same App Group filenames**: `MapSnapshot-<deviceID>-light.png` / `-dark.png`. If app-side snapshot generation runs with *older cached data* (or simply later), it can overwrite the widget’s newer snapshot → widget text (fresh server fetch) updates, but the file on disk is now stale/incorrect.

- **H2 – WidgetKit execution budget / detached task not finishing**  
  The widget triggers snapshot generation in a `Task.detached` and doesn’t await it. WidgetKit may suspend/kill the extension before snapshot writing finishes, so the widget shows new text (payload updated) but still loads an older PNG.

- **H3 – Staleness check passes even though content is wrong**  
  The widget decides “snapshot is fresh” using **file modification date** vs timestamp. If a different process overwrote the file recently with wrong content, the modDate is “fresh” but the pixels are not.

- **H4 – Read/replace timing and SwiftUI view refresh**  
  You read the PNG synchronously with `Data(contentsOf:)`. If the file is replaced right after the read, the view may keep showing the old decoded `UIImage` until the next timeline render.

### What can be done to prevent it (after we confirm which hypothesis is real)

The fix will depend on which hypothesis the logs confirm, but the high-probability direction is:
- **Single writer / single source of truth** for snapshot files (avoid app + widget writing the same filenames), or
- **Versioned filenames** (e.g., include a payload version/timestamp in the filename) so stale overwrites can’t “win”, and the widget always loads the image that matches the entry it’s showing.

### I added instrumentation (no behavior changes yet)

I added **8 small NDJSON logs** covering:
- widget selected device/timestamp
- detached snapshot task start
- snapshot staleness decision + file mod dates
- snapshot render start + write complete
- widget PNG load (what file/bytes/modDate it actually read)
- app snapshot render/write (to detect overwrites)

Now we need a reproduction run to collect evidence.

3. Trigger location changes/updates as you normally do (or via Xcode’s Simulate Location), until you observe: **widget text/distance updates but the map image is clearly wrong/stale**.
4. After you see the mismatch, stop interacting and wait ~10 seconds so any snapshot task has time to attempt a write.</reproduction_steps>
